label: Produced by a bearer: an item the bearer makes as something other than itself
term: produced by a bearer (Produces b e)
definition: Produces b e: the bearer b produces the item e as something other than itself, for example an abstract object or a realm of possibles that the source makes and that then exists alongside it. It is production only, not every grounding relation: an item grounded in b without being made by b (a mode of b's own nature, a value-fact grounded in b's nature) is not thereby produced, and if it is an intrinsic determination of b it is contained. Examples: on theistic activism, abstract objects that God creates; on a Plotinian reading, Intellect and its forms as the product of the One (navigation only). Non-examples: an intrinsic determination of b (that is containment); an item independent of b. Structural properties: a declared primitive two-place relation; intended irreflexive (nothing produces itself) and, among produced items, asymmetric; neither property is assumed in Lean. It is not linked in Lean to the CausalityFrame relations CausesIn or GivesAt; reading it as one of them would be an explicit open bridge. It is not exclusive of containment in the type.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 premise lane C), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Individuating non-present candidates: the axiarchic rival and the cognition criterion'. Lean has no declaration for it: it is the parameter Produces : B → C → Prop.
